page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top, with the page number at top left. Centred heading "CONCIO VIII." with the scripture reference "Genef. 21." below it. Then one block of italic text, set in one paragraph with a woodcut initial. Catchword at the lower right.

l.i: VISITAVIT autem Domi-
nus Saram, quemadmodum
dixerat: fecitq; dominus Sa-
ra, sicut loquutus fuerat. Nam
concepit & peperit Sara ipsi Abraham
filium in senectute sua, idq; illo tempore,
quod prædixerat ei Deus. Et Abraham
vocauit nomen filii sui, qui sibi natus e-
rat, & quem sibi genuerat Sara, Isahac.
Circumcidit quoque Abraham Isahac
filium suum, cum esset filius octo dierum,
quemadmodum præceperat illi Deus. Por-
rò Abraham fuit filius centum annorum,
cum sibi nasceretur Isahac filius suus. Sa-
ra verò dixit: risum fecit mihi Deus, ut
omnis qui audierit, corrideat mihi. Di-
xitq;, quis unquam dixit Abraha, lacta-
uit Sara filios? siquidem genvi filium in
senectute illius. Creuit itaque puer &
ablactatus est, fecitq; Abraham convi-
vium magnum illo die cum ablactaretur
Isahac. Et vidit Sara filium Hagar Ae-
gyptia, quem illa genuit ipsi Abraham,
esse derisorem. Unde dixit ad Abraham:
eijce[?]

page.notes: The woodcut initial V is joined to "ISITAVIT", so it reads "VISITAVIT". "Abraham" is printed with a small sign before the name, which I have not reproduced. "eijce" at the foot is the catchword. Its last letters are hard to read, so I marked them with [?]. Changes from the printed spelling: "Creuit" is written "Creuit" as printed, "genuerat" and "genui" are printed with u, "conuiuium" is printed with uiu, and u/v and i/j are normalised where a consonant or vowel was clear. Where the printed form was uncertain, I kept the printed letters.
